topics.title: OrcaSlicer 2.5 Is Out, Plugins and All
topics.description: The stable release landed November 7, and a wave of free community plugins showed up within two days

slides.heading: OrcaSlicer 2.5 Is Out, Plugins and All
slides.body: Stable release, November 7. The team calls it the biggest update in Orca's history: nearly 1,300 pull requests from more than 180 contributors.
bullets: Python plugins, with a community plugin hub
Belt-printer slicing and color mixing from loaded filaments
Texture displacement and an experimental Design tab
Print two to four parts at once on IDEX printers
Bambu H2C and A2L support; mixed nozzle sizes on H2D and X2D

slides.heading: Before You Upgrade
bullets: Bambu process presets now default to Grid infill, not Cross Hatch
Plugins are not sandboxed. Only install ones you trust
Windows builds are now signed
Since the beta: bridges print at bridge speed again, scarf seams stop banding

slides.heading: The First Plugins
bullets: Color Split: cut a painted model into one part per color, no AMS needed
Flow Line Art: print a photo as one spiral line
Print Memory and Klipper Sync: learn from your Klipper history, catch bad settings
Head Room: fit a cosplay helmet to your head before printing
All brand new and barely tested. Read the code first

slides.heading: Also New in Software
bullets: Bambuddy 1.3.0: the free Bambu farm manager adds per-print archives and staff approval
Queued jobs now wait for the right filament instead of printing the wrong one
PrusaSlicer 3.0 alpha 14 fixes alpha 13's MMU crashes

topics.title: Prusa Owners: Update Your Firmware
topics.description: A researcher took over his own MK4S over the network. Buddy firmware 7.0.0 and newer fix it on 15 Prusa models

slides.heading: Prusa Owners: Update Your Firmware
slides.body: Researcher Yannick Dixken spent a week attacking his own MK4S with an AI model and a fuzzer. He found 14 issues and ended up running his own code on the printer. Prusa fixed them all in Buddy firmware 7.0.0.
bullets: Affected: CORE One family, XL, MK4/MK4S, MK3.9, MK3.5 and MINI
Fix: firmware 7.0.0 or newer (8.0.0 includes it)
Prusa knows of no real-world attacks. Exploit code is expected in December

slides.heading: What to Do Tonight
bullets: Check the firmware on every printer, not just one
Keep printers off the open internet. Use a VPN for remote access
Leave TLS on for Prusa Connect
Don't print from USB sticks you didn't set up yourself
Side story: Prusa held back the open-source code for weeks, then called that "the wrong call"

topics.title: Kickstarter Week: Three New Printers
topics.description: A four-toolhead printer launching today, InfiMech's MX past two million dollars, and a resin printer that washes its own prints

slides.heading: Kickstarter Week: Three New Printers
slides.body: Three crowdfunded printers in one week. Kickstarter is a pledge, not a store: delivery dates slip and refunds aren't guaranteed.
bullets: Co Print Quadro: four toolheads, from $649, live today
InfiMech MX: from $299, over $2 million raised
UniFormation S10: resin that washes and dries itself, about $999

slides.heading: Co Print Quadro: Four Toolheads, $649
bullets: Live on Kickstarter today, 11 AM Eastern
Four separate toolheads, about a 1-second swap, up to 90% less waste
300 mm cube, 600 mm/s, hardened steel nozzles
$649 Super Early Bird (retail $899). Shipping planned from February 2027

slides.heading: InfiMech MX: $2.1 Million in Three Days
bullets: Live since November 10, ends December 10
Over $2.1 million from about 2,870 backers (goal: $51,000)
MX from $299, MX Pro from $549 (later tiers cost more)
No delivery date published yet

slides.heading: UniFormation S10: Resin That Cleans Itself
bullets: After printing, the part moves into a built-in 9-liter wash tank, then warm-air dries
16K screen, 223 × 126 × 200 mm build volume
About $999 pledge. Over $630,000 raised, ends December 1
Limits: curing is a $30 add-on, supports still come off by hand
Ships March 2027

topics.title: Printers for the Family: $329 and $349
topics.description: Creality's kid-run mBox and QIDI's MakeBuddy Smart5 both launched this week, just in time for holiday shopping

slides.heading: Printers for the Family: $329 and $349
slides.body: Two enclosed starter printers for kids and families launched the same week. Same idea, different trade-offs.
bullets: Creality mBox: $329, TikTok Shop only, promo through December 10
QIDI MakeBuddy Smart5: $349 on QIDI's store
Both enclosed, both app-driven, both aimed at holiday gifts

slides.heading: mBox vs. Smart5
bullets: Build size: 153 mm cube vs. 180 mm cube
Materials: PLA only vs. PLA and PETG
Heated bed: no vs. yes
Where to buy: TikTok Shop vs. QIDI's own store
Smart5 comes with four spools and two DIY kits

topics.title: Formnext Next Week + Bambu Circle
topics.description: Teasers ahead of the big show in Frankfurt, November 17 to 20, and Bambu's plan to certify local print shops

slides.heading: Formnext Next Week + Bambu Circle
slides.body: Formnext runs November 17 to 20 in Frankfurt. Expect reveals next week; here's what's been teased.
bullets: Elegoo: an upgraded resin printer plus one unnamed machine
Snapmaker: a U1 top cover, a color-mixing filament bundle, a model library
Bambu: H3C and the R1 laser on show

slides.heading: Bambu Circle: Certified Local Print Shops
bullets: Bambu will train and certify local partners to fix printers, sell, print and teach
Pilot in the Netherlands; Germany and France in early 2027
Goal: a certified partner within an hour's drive of every European user
Waiting list is open now. No costs or US plans announced

topics.title: Robotics Corner: Greg the High-Five Robot
topics.description: A printed five-servo arm whose CAD, firmware and vision code an AI wrote, plus a litter-picking rover and a chess-fixing arm

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: Greg the High-Five Robot
slides.body: Hold up an open palm and Greg reaches out and slaps it. Andris Gauracs printed and built it; Claude Code wrote the CAD, the firmware and the vision code. MIT license. Image: Andris Gauracs / high-five-robot.

slides.heading: What Goes Into Greg
bullets: A tiny ESP32 camera streams video; your computer spots a raised palm
A second ESP32 drives five hobby servos
About $140 to $230 in parts
PLA or PETG, 0.2 mm layers, no supports, fits a 225 mm bed

slides.heading: MOSS: A Printed Litter-Picking Rover
bullets: Tracked rover with printed TPU tracks and an SO-101-style arm
About $460 in base parts, $600 to $1,390 with a computer and cameras
Drives and picks things up today; litter picking on its own isn't shown yet
Builder's tip this week: thicker charging wires, the thin ones got warm

slides.heading: An Arm That Fixes Your Chess Board
bullets: An SO-101 picks up knocked-over pieces and stands them back on their squares
Within 4 mm, and the gripper camera checks each piece
No AI training: just a fast motion library, small enough for an ESP32

topics.title: AI Corner: Praxis-1 Learned From SO-101s
topics.description: Runway's open robot model trained partly on thousands of hobbyist SO-101 recordings, a free no-code course, and Claude designing gadgets

slides.heading: AI Corner: Praxis-1 Learned From SO-101s
slides.body: Runway, the AI video company, released Praxis-1 on November 11: a free, open robot model. Part of its training came from robot-arm recordings that hobbyists uploaded to Hugging Face.
bullets: 3,956 public SO-100/SO-101 datasets from 1,783 people
Maybe some of yours
Apache-2.0, works with LeRobot
An SO-101 version came out today

slides.heading: The Catch: A Big Graphics Card
bullets: Running it needs a GPU with at least 80 GB of memory
The full model is 54 GB; a smaller version is 17.5 GB
Runway lists Jetson Thor and RTX 5090 as targets

slides.heading: No GPU? Viam's Free Course
bullets: Teach your SO-101 to move a mug, with no code and no graphics card
Record demos, train in Viam's cloud for free, run it on your arm
About 1 hour with their model, about 5 hours with your own demos
Mac (Apple Silicon) or Linux. No Windows yet

slides.heading: Claude Designed Three Working Gadgets
bullets: Anthropic's new Claude Fable 5.2 went from a one-paragraph prompt to a working device
Specs, circuit boards, firmware and 3D-printable cases
A speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub and a handheld virtual pet
All three worked without electrical fixes. Early prototypes, not products

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Kevin Kuehn's PETG Car
topics.description: A road-legal electric car with a body printed from 600+ pieces of PETG, and the free tool he built to split it

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Kevin Kuehn's PETG Car
slides.body: A road-legal, registered electric car in California. The body is 3D printed: more than 600 PETG pieces from three printers running around the clock for about a month.

slides.heading: How He Built It
bullets: Designed in Fusion, checked for strength and airflow before printing
About 8 mm PETG shell, joined with heat staples, then skinned in carbon fiber
Nissan Leaf motor and battery, Miata suspension and steering
Two seats front to back, under 2,000 lb

slides.heading: Try It: Section3D
bullets: The free tool he wrote to split the body
Cuts any oversized model into support-free pieces that fit your bed
Numbers the parts, adds dowel holes, packs the plates
Exports 3MFs plus a PDF assembly guide
Windows, open source (GPL-3.0)
